shared_elements: carved stone monument displayed in a museum interior
anthropomorphic head/figure with a broad headdress-like element on top
sets of incised parallel grooves suggesting hair or feathers
justification: Both are tall, top-heavy stone monuments in which a broad, fan-like headdress with fine incised parallel grooves sits above a bulkier body mass, and both are displayed as unpainted weathered stone in gallery lighting. The decisive difference is the mode of carving: A is a single flat-fronted slab covered in shallow low-relief motifs (disc, bands, curvilinear devices) on an unbroken surface, while B is a fully volumetric, deeply undercut composition of stacked blocky masses with almost no surface ornament.
